`*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n23\t    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n24\t    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n25\t    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n26\t        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n27\t        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n28\t\n29\t        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n30\t        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n31\t        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n32\t        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n33\t            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n34\t        } else {\n35\t            pattern.clone()\n36\t        };\n37\t\n38\t        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n39\t\n40\t        Ok(CompiledRule {\n41\t            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n42\t            adapter,\n43\t        })\n44\t    }\n45\t\n46\t    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n47\t    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n48\t        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n49\t    }\n50\t}\n51\t\n52\t/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n53\t///\n54\t/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n55\t/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n56\t/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n57\t///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n58\t/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n59\t/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\n60\tfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n61\t    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n62\t    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n63\t    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n64\t        matches!(c, '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\')\n65\t    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n66\t\n67\t    if has_regex_features {\n68\t        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n69\t        return false;\n70\t    }\n71\t\n72\t    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n73\t    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n74\t    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n75\t    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n76\t    let mut i = 0;\n77\t\n78\t    while i < chars.len() {\n79\t        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n80\t            // Skip escaped character.\n81\t            i += 2;\n82\t            continue;\n83\t        }\n84\t        if chars[i] == '*' {\n85\t            return true;\n86\t        }\n87\t        i += 1;\n88\t    }\n89\t\n90\t    false\n91\t}\n92\t\n93\t/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n94\t///\n95\t/// Rules:\n96\t/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n97\t/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n98\t/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n99\t/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n100\t/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\n101\tfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n102\t    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n103\t    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n104\t        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n105\t    }\n106\t\n107\t    let mut result = String::new();\n108\t    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n109\t    let mut i = 0;\n110\t\n111\t    while i < chars.len() {\n112\t        match chars[i] {\n113\t            '\\\\' => {\n114\t                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n115\t                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n116\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n117\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n118\t                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n119\t                    i += 2;\n120\t                } else {\n121\t                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n122\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n123\t                    i += 1;\n124\t                }\n125\t            }\n126\t            '*' => {\n127\t                // Check for **.\n128\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n129\t                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n130\t                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n131\t                    i += 2;\n132\t                } else {\n133\t                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n134\t                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n135\t                    i += 1;\n136\t                }\n137\t            }\n138\t            c => {\n139\t                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n140\t                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n141\t                // the glob conversion.\n142\t                result.push(c);\n143\t                i += 1;\n144\t            }\n145\t        }\n146\t    }\n147\t\n148\t    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n149\t    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n150\t}\n151\t\n152\t/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n153\t///\n154\t/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n155\t/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n156\t///\n157\t/// # Arguments\n158\t///\n159\t/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n160\t/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n161\t/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n162\t///\n163\t/// # Returns\n164\t///\n165\t/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n166\t/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n167\t///\n168\t/// # Examples\n169\t///\n170\t/// ```\n171\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n172\t/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n173\t///\n174\t/// let rules = vec![\n175\t///     RoutingRule {\n176\t///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n177\t///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n178\t///     },\n179\t///     RoutingRule {\n180\t///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n181\t///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n182\t///     },\n183\t/// ];\n184\t///\n185\t/// // First rule matches.\n186\t/// assert_eq!(\n187\t///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n188\t///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n189\t/// );\n190\t///\n191\t/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n192\t/// assert_eq!(\n193\t///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n194\t///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n195\t/// );\n196\t/// ```\n197\tpub fn match_adapter(\n198\t    model: &str,\n199\t    rules: &[RoutingRule],\n200\t    default: &str,\n201\t) -> Option<String> {\n202\t    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n203\t    for rule in rules {\n204\t        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n205\t            Ok(compiled) => {\n206\t                if compiled.matches(model) {\n207\t                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n208\t                }\n209\t            }\n210\t            Err(e) => {\n211\t                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n212\t                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n213\t                tracing::warn!(\n214\t                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n215\t                    error = %e,\n216\t                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n217\t                );\n218\t            }\n219\t        }\n220\t    }\n221\t\n222\t    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n223\t    if default.is_empty() {\n224\t        None\n225\t    } else {\n226\t        Some(default.to_string())\n227\t    }\n228\t}\n229\t\n230\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n231\t// Tests\n232\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n233\t\n234\t#[cfg(test)]\n235\tmod tests {\n236\t    use super::*;\n237\t    use crate::config::RoutingRule;\n238\t\n239\t    fn make_rule(pattern: &str, adapter: &str) -> RoutingRule {\n240\t        RoutingRule {\n241\t            match_model: pattern.to_string(),\n242\t Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(c, '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\')\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(\n    model: &str,\n    rules: &[RoutingRule],\n    default: &str,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Where a configuration value originated.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ConfigSource {\n    /// Built-in default value.\n    Default,\n    /// Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`).\n    GlobalFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml`).\n    WorkspaceFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Environment variable override.\n    EnvVar(String),\n    /// CLI argument override.\n    CliOverride,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigSource {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ConfigSource::Default => write!(f, \"built-in default\"),\n            ConfigSource::GlobalFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::EnvVar(name) => write!(f, \"{} env var\", name),\n            ConfigSource::CliOverride => write!(f, \"CLI argument\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map of config field paths to their source.\n///\n/// Used by `needle config --dump --show-source` to annotate each value.\npub type SourceMap = BTreeMap<String, ConfigSource>;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Workspace Overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single config validation error.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ConfigError {\n    /// Dot-separated field path (e.g., `agent.default`).\n    pub field: String,\n    /// Human-readable explanation.\n    pub message: String,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigError {\n    fn ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// CLI overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// CLI-level ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Loads and validates NEEDLE configuration.\npub struct ConfigLoader;\n\nimpl ConfigLoader {\n    /// Load global config from `~/.config/needle/config.yaml`.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config (not an error).\n    pub fn load_global() -> Result<Config> {\n        let path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n        Self::load_from_path(&path)\n    }\n\n    /// Load config from a specific path.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config.\n    pub fn load_from_path(path: &Path) -> Result<Config> {\n        if !path.exists() {\n            return Ok(Config::default());\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        let config: Config = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(config)\n    }\n\n    /// Load workspace overrides from `.needle.yaml` in the given workspace root.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if the file does not exist. Emits warnings for\n    /// non-overridable keys found in the workspace config.\n    pub fn load_workspace(workspace_root: &Path) -> Result<Option<WorkspaceOverrides>> {\n        let path = workspace_root.join(\".needle.yaml\");\n        if !path.exists() {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        // Check for non-overridable keys and warn.\n        Self::warn_non_overridable_keys(&text, &path)?;\n\n        let overrides: WorkspaceOverrides = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(Some(overrides))\n    }\n\n    /// Warn about non-overridable top-level keys in workspace config YAML.\n    fn warn_non_overridable_keys(yaml_text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n        let value: serde_yaml::Value = serde_yaml::from_str(yaml_text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        if let serde_yaml::Value::Mapping(map) = value {\n            for key in map.keys() {\n                if let serde_yaml::Value::String(key_str) = key {\n                    if NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS.contains(&key_str.as_str()) {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            key = %key_str,\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            \"workspace config contains non-overridable setting '{}' — ignored\",\n                            key_str,\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Apply workspace overrides to a config.\n    ///\n    /// Only overridable fields are applied. Records sources in the source map.\n    pub fn apply_workspace(\n        config: &mut Config,\n        overrides: &WorkspaceOverrides,\n        ws_path: &Path,\n        sources: &mut SourceMap,\n    ) {\n        let source = ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(ws_path.join(\".needle.yaml\"));\n\n        if let Some(ref agent) = overrides.agent {\n            if let Some(ref default) = agent.default {\n                config.agent.default = default.clone();\n                sources.insert(\"agent.default\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(timeout) = agent.timeout {\n                config.agent.timeout = timeout;\n                sources.insert(\"agent.timeout\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref routing) = agent.routing {\n                config.agent.routing = Some(routing.clone());\n                sources.insert(\"agent.routing\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref strands) = overrides.strands {\n            if let Some(ref weave_val) = strands.weave {\n                if let Ok(weave_cfg) = serde_yaml::from_value::<WeaveConfig>(weave_val.clone()) {\n                    config.strands.weave = weave_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.weave\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref pulse_val) = strands.pulse {\n                if let Ok(pulse_cfg) = serde_yaml::from_value::<PulseConfig>(pulse_val.clone()) {\n                    config.strands.pulse = pulse_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.pulse\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref unravel_val) = strands.unravel {\n                if let Ok(unravel_cfg) =\n                    serde_yaml::from_value::<UnravelConfig>(unravel_val.clone())\n                {\n                    config.strands.unravel = unravel_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.unravel\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref prompt) = overrides.prompt {\n            config.prompt = prompt.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"prompt.context_files\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            sources.insert(\"prompt.instructions\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref verification) = overrides.verification {\n            config.verification = verification.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"verification\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref gates) = overrides.gates {\n            config.gates = gates.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"gates\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref ws) = overrides.workspace {\n            if !ws.labels.is_empty() {\n                config.workspace.labels = ws.labels.clone();\n                sources.insert(\"workspace.labels\".to_string(), source);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply environment variable overrides (`NEEDLE_*` prefix, `__` separator).\n    ///\n    /// Example: `NEEDLE_AGENT__DEFAULT=opus` sets `agent.default` to `\"opus\"`.\n    pub fn apply_env_overrides(config: &mut Config, sources: &mut SourceMap) {\n        for (key, value) in std::env::vars() {\n            if let Some(suffix) = key.strip_prefix(\"NEEDLE_\") {\n                let config_path = suffix.to_lowercase().replace(\"__\", \".\");\n                let source = ConfigSource::EnvVar(key.clone());\n\n                match config_path.as_str() {\n                    \"agent.default\" => {\n                        config.agent.default = value;\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"agent.timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.agent.timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for agent.timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"agent.routing.default_adapter\" => {\n                        config\n                            .agent\n                            .routing\n                            .get_or_insert_with(RoutingConfig::default)\n                            .default_adapter = Some(value);\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"worker.max_workers\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u32>() {\n                            config.worker.max_workers = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.max_workers — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"worker.idle_timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.worker.idle_timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.idle_timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"worker.launch_stagger_seconds\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.launch_stagger_seconds — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"health.heartbeat_interval_secs\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for health.heartbeat_interval_secs — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for health.heartbeat_ttl_secs — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"self_modification.enabled\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) =
